Like Le Mans, it'll be on Motor Trend's pay app/site. You can just grab it for 14 days and cancel. If you grabbed it last week for Le Mans, it's still in the free trial stage. I don't actually remember what it costs, but it's something low. It's only like 6 bucks a month, or under 30 bucks for the entire year. It's well worth the cost - for me.

But, the free trial works and you still have 8 days left if you signed up last Saturday for the free trial and to watch Le Mans. I want to say coverage begins at like 03:00 Eastern US time. There's free streaming on YouTube of what's going on at the Nordschleife this weekend. The race may well be streamed by "ADAC Nurburgring" or the "Nurbergring" channel on YouTube. I don't know yet and won't know until either tomorrow or until someone lazier than me asks me to go look and find them a stream.

This 24 hour race is on the "Green Hell." It has been going on since like 1970 - almost 50 years now. Unlike every other 24 hour race, this race is considered to be on a track that is equivalent to the same terrain you'll find on a real road. (For some reason, I'm not sure why, Bathurst isn't considered to be one.)

Anyhow, it will be mayhem! There's gonna be at least 200 cars starting the race around the 13ish mile circuit. For much of the track, the slightest off WILL result in hitting something hard.

And, best of all, it's mayhem. It is, too! LOL There's multiple classes on the track. You've got everything from prototypes going 300ish kph to GT4 cars going 250 kph. Hell, they might even have TCR on the track, rocking it out at not much more than 200 kph.

They all drive on the same track, for 24 hours... Yup.... It's awesome! They all fuel at different intervals, so the pits are mayhem. There's going to be at least 700 different drivers.

I haven't looked, but BMW uses the track for testing and has their own center right there at the track. So, even though they're winding down the GT program for the Hypercar class that's coming, I kind of expect them to at least make a slight effort - even if for tradition or because it's their last go-round.

Anyhow, I'm gonna watch the race, as much as I can. It should be over by the time I have to leave on Sunday. I'll make a thread tomorrow for those of us who watch it - or one of you lazy bastards can make the damned thread.
